topics.label: Introduction and learning outcomes for the hallmarks of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: This opening section sets out the lecture aims and introduces the hallmarks of cancer framework.

topics.label: Growth signaling pathways and oncogenic mutations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how oncogenic mutations across membrane receptor signaling pathways confer autonomous proliferation and survival signals.

topics.label: Block to terminal differentiation in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how failure to complete terminal differentiation preserves proliferative progenitor states in hematopoietic and epithelial tissues.

topics.label: Resistance to apoptosis, replicative immortality, and p53 regulation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how cancer cells bypass intrinsic growth-limiting checkpoints, cell death, and senescence through telomere maintenance and p53 pathway deregulation.

topics.label: Cancer metabolism, the Warburg effect, and oncometabolites
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how cancer cells alter their metabolic wiring and generate oncometabolites to support biosynthetic demands and epigenetic regulation.

topics.label: Tumor angiogenesis and the angiogenic switch
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic addresses how tumors overcome diffusion limits to stimulate new blood vessel growth.

topics.label: Mechanisms, detection, and genomics of tumor metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the biological hurdles of cancer dissemination, circulating tumor cell monitoring, and the genomic features of secondary metastatic sites.

topics.label: Summary and concluding remarks
topics.groupedBecause: This closing section summarises the key themes of the lecture and provides concluding administrative remarks.
